result: Observed tight triple uncertainty relations that are stronger than those derived from pairwise relations, confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence for fundamental triple uncertainty relations, advancing the understanding of quantum incompatibility and its implications for quantum information.

title: Equilibrium Thermometry In The Multilevel Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Tabitha Doicin, Luis A. Correa, Jonas Glatthard, Andrew D. Armour, and Gerardo Adesso

The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the temperature sensitivity of a quantum probe in equilibrium using the quantum Rabi model, finding that degeneracy enhances sensitivity while uniform spectra broaden the operating range.
motivation: Quantum thermometry at the nanoscale is crucial for applications, and understanding how probe structure affects sensitivity is key to designing optimal thermometers.
method: The authors compute the thermal quantum Fisher information for the multilevel quantum Rabi model, analyzing the effects of energy-level degeneracy and spectral uniformity on temperature estimation precision.
result: Degenerate energy levels lead to higher peak sensitivity, while a more uniform spectrum maintains sensitivity over a broader temperature range.
conclusion: The quantum Rabi model provides a tunable platform for equilibrium thermometry, with trade-offs between peak sensitivity and operating range that can be exploited for specific applications.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops Weingarten calculus for real Clifford group to study anticoncentration and state design properties of doped real Clifford circuits and tensor networks.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of quantum circuits with magic resources is crucial for quantum advantage and complexity theory; real Clifford circuits are relevant to many physical platforms.
method: Derives exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, and analyzes anticoncentration and state design properties under magic doping.
result: Identifies a different universality class for real stabilizer states compared to complex ones, and characterizes how doping with magic resources leads to approximate state designs.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous framework for analyzing real Clifford circuits, with implications for quantum advantage and tensor network simulations.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, using a statistical-gauge geometry to derive sum rules and Ward identities.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints like sum rules and Ward identities are hard to expose due to distributional currents and anomaly-like contact terms; a systematic geometric organization is needed.
method: The authors propose a statistical-gauge geometry that organizes the recently identified constraints, providing a simple geometric picture for deriving these identities.
result: The geometric framework yields a clear derivation of sum rules and Ward identities, clarifying the role of contact terms and anomalies.
conclusion: This geometric approach offers a unified and intuitive understanding of equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, with potential applications to non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and work fluctuations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and a second-law-like inequality for nonreciprocal systems, showing that entropy production can be negative in transient regimes.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to analyze nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret communication protocol using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing how information can be encoded and transmitted.
result: The protocol enables robust secret communication that leaves no locally detectable traces, achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: Paraparticles offer a new resource for quantum communication with unique security properties.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the scalability of gradients in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogation method to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering scalability. The paper aims to understand the conditions under which gradients remain trainable and to develop a method to avoid barren plateaus.
method: The authors analyze gradient scaling in VQAs and introduce a Taylor surrogation technique that approximates the cost function locally to provide non-vanishing gradients, enabling efficient optimization.
result: They show that the proposed Taylor surrogation can circumvent barren plateaus for certain ansätze and that the gradient scaling relates to the expressibility of the quantum circuit.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to improve trainability of VQAs and offers insights into the relationship between circuit expressibility and gradient behavior.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing with intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; existing entangled states are fragile to such noise.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are naturally insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust against common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging noise-robust entangled states.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of motion are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with engineered spin-motion coupling and optimal control to prepare target superpositions of Fock states and squeezed states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying nonclassicality via Wigner function negativity.
conclusion: The technique provides a versatile toolbox for quantum state engineering in trapped ions, with applications in metrology and quantum information processing.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical readout and manipulation without destroying the circular state.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states (ionization) is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors use experimental techniques to probe excited-state dynamics, identifying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions that lead to transmon ionization.
result: They characterize the ionization process and its dependence on experimental parameters, revealing the mechanisms by which qubits leak into higher energy levels.
conclusion: Controlling transmon ionization is essential for high-fidelity readout and error mitigation in superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts induced by ionizing radiation in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, using state-of-the-art radiation protection and analyzing error correlations.
result: They discover a new type of correlated error—phase error bursts—that occur even with radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Radiation-induced correlated phase errors pose a significant challenge for fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction method that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to define an effective reduced model.
result: The technique accurately reproduces the observable dynamics of the original system with significantly fewer degrees of freedom.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems, bridging microscopic models and observed dynamics.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating and exploiting spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and experimentally realize a protocol using spin-dependent squeezing in a trapped-ion system to achieve Heisenberg-limited displacement sensing.
result: They achieve optimal sensitivity for displacement measurements, surpassing the standard quantum limit and demonstrating the utility of spin-dependent squeezed states.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function negativity. They develop theoretical tools to compute it for various state classes.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression. Examples include cat states and photon-added states.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, with applications in resource theory and quantum information processing with continuous variables.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding the origins of decoherence is crucial for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing spectroscopy and noise characterization to identify mechanisms causing spectral diffusion and linewidth broadening.
result: They identify specific noise sources, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, that dominate spectral instability, and quantify their impact on emitter coherence.
conclusion: Mitigating identified noise sources can significantly improve the spectral stability of erbium emitters, advancing their use in quantum repeaters and network nodes.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, outperforming standard methods in efficiency and accuracy.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a practical tool for quantum estimation tasks, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays stabilize exotic non-equilibrium phases such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg atoms with long-range interactions, analyzing the interplay of cavity-mediated coupling and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints give rise to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phenomena in a hybrid quantum system.
conclusion: The work establishes cavity-QED with Rydberg arrays as a platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, accounting for experimental constraints.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits with random measurements and shows that measurement outcomes can improve decoding of quantum error-correcting codes.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and fault tolerance, particularly how measurement data can aid decoding in monitored dynamics.
method: The authors analyze random quantum circuits with interspersed measurements, using statistical mechanics mappings and tensor network techniques to study decoding transitions.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, leading to new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes exhibit improved error correction capabilities when measurement outcomes are used, suggesting new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve strong blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from low fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action approach combined with computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling systematic improvement of the driving Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum state transfer and other control tasks compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly higher bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These enhanced mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction codes must be tailored.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware constraints such as long-range interactions and parallel gate operations.
result: The architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit overhead, and runtime compared to standard surface-code-based approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can efficiently support large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation with practical overhead, making them a promising platform for near-term quantum advantage.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or target only uncorrelated noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic generation of sequences that cancel k-local correlated noise.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits and are tailored to specific noise models, offering efficient suppression of spatially correlated errors.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, providing a practical tool for improving coherence in multi-qubit systems.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: Understanding hidden subgroup structures in quantum states is fundamental for quantum algorithm design and learning theory.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and stabilizer formalism to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and more general Abelian hidden subgroups from quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithm design and complexity theory.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum computers.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from demolition errors and long readout times, limiting qudit performance. The authors aim to enhance measurement fidelity while preserving the quantum state.
method: They implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, applied to a silicon quantum dot qudit platform.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% with reduced measurement time and significantly fewer measurement-induced errors compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a powerful technique for high-fidelity, nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qudit platforms and relevant for quantum computing and sensing.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, using a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used to simulate variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and high-rate key distribution.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, squeezed states, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (finite-size, composable), and experimental implementations.
result: CV quantum communication is now a mature field with record key rates over metropolitan distances, and security proofs have reached a level comparable to discrete-variable systems.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work to extend distance via repeaters and improve integration.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, addressing their limitations and experimental feasibility.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, quantum digital signatures) and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It categorizes quantum crypto primitives, explains their security models, and highlights experimental progress and challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant limitations that require further theoretical and experimental advances.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behavior using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct types of universality in driven open matter, linking them to underlying theoretical concepts.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive classification that can guide future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further work is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, as standard quantum theory and classical gravity are incompatible; information-theoretic methods provide a framework to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two quantum probes, analyzing the constraints such experiments would place on any new theory of gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity using current or near-future technology, with detailed analysis of their requirements and potential outcomes.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, and GIE experiments are promising candidates for laboratory-based tests.

title: Simulating Magic State Cultivation With Few Clifford Terms
authors: Kwok Ho Wan, Zhenghao Zhong, And Ainhoa Zapirain
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2134 (2026).

Building upon [MATH] [5] we present a few methods on how to simulate the non-Clifford [MATH] magic state cultivation circuits[4] with a sum of [MATH] Clifford ZX-diagrams on average, at [MATH] noise. Compared to a magic cat state stabiliser decomposition of all [MATH] non-Clifford spiders ([MATH] terms required), this is more than [MATH] times reduction in the number of terms. Our stabiliser decomposition has the advantage of representing the final non-Clifford state (in light of circuit errors) as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams. This will be useful in simulating the escape stage of magic state cultivation, where one needs to port the resultant state of cultivation into a larger Clifford circuit with many more qubits. Still, it's necessary to only track [MATH] Clifford terms. Our result sheds light on the simulability of operationally relevant, high [MATH]-count quantum circuits with some internal structure. Finally, we provide numerical results for full non-Clifford stabiliser rank simulation based on [MATH] along with optimisations using our cutting decompositions. Nearly [MATH] shots per second can be obtained on a laptop for the smaller [MATH] circuits at uniform circuit level noise [MATH], making it only [MATH][MATH] times slower than its (circuit-unspecific and un-optimised) fully Clifford proxy simulation via [MATH] using [MATH] gates.

.
tldr: Presents methods to simulate magic state cultivation circuits using a sum of few Clifford ZX-diagrams, achieving a significant reduction in non-Clifford terms.
motivation: Magic state cultivation is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these circuits is costly due to high non-Clifford count. Efficient simulation methods are needed to analyze and optimize such circuits.
method: The authors develop stabiliser decompositions that represent the non-Clifford state as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams, leveraging the structure of cultivation circuits to reduce the number of terms compared to a naive decomposition.
result: They achieve more than a 1000-fold reduction in the number of terms, enabling simulation of small cultivation circuits at near-Clifford speeds on a laptop.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that operationally relevant high T-count circuits with internal structure can be simulated efficiently, aiding the development of magic state cultivation protocols.

title: Long-time Freeness In The Kicked Top
authors: Elisa Vallini And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2129 (2026).

Recent work highlighted the importance of higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics for a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization. The full Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis, the framework encompassing correlations, can be formalized using the language of Free Probability theory. In this context, chaotic dynamics at long times are proposed to lead to free independence or "freeness" of observables. In this work, we investigate these issues in a paradigmatic semiclassical model – the kicked top – which exhibits a transition from integrability to chaos. Despite its simplicity, we identify several non-trivial features. By numerically studying 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators, we show that in the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast. These considerations lead us to introduce a large deviation theory for freeness that enables us to define and analyze the associated time scale. The numerical results confirm the existence of a hierarchy of different time scales, indicating a multifractal approach to freeness in this model. Our findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for the study of many-body quantum dynamics.

.
tldr: This paper studies the approach to freeness in the kicked top model, revealing exponential convergence and a hierarchy of time scales in chaotic dynamics.
motivation: Understanding higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics is crucial for a deeper theory of quantum chaos and thermalization, and free probability provides a natural framework.
method: The authors numerically compute 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators in the kicked top model across integrable and chaotic regimes, and develop a large deviation theory for freeness.
result: In the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast, and the associated time scales exhibit a multifractal hierarchy.
conclusion: The findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic quantum systems and may have broader implications for many-body quantum dynamics.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical quantum oblivious transfer protocol with simulation security based on one-way functions, designed for experimental feasibility.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical due to high resource requirements or security assumptions.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitment and one-way functions to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for error correction and resource estimation.
result: The protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency and provides explicit error correction methods, making it suitable for experimental realization.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum cryptography by offering a feasible QOT protocol, though it relies on computational assumptions (one-way functions) rather than full device independence.

title: Exact Distinguishability Between Real-valued And Complex-valued Haar Random Quantum States
authors: Tristan Nemoz, Romain Alléaume, And Peter Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2120 (2026).

Haar random states are fundamental objects in quantum information theory and quantum computing. We study the density matrix resulting from sampling [MATH] copies of a [MATH]-dimensional quantum state according to the Haar measure on the orthogonal group. In particular, we analytically compute its spectral decomposition. This allows us to compute exactly the trace distance between [MATH]-copies of a real Haar random state and [MATH]-copies of a complex Haar random state. Using this we show a lower-bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state [MATH]-designs and improve the lower-bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.

.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral decomposition of the density matrix of multiple copies of Haar random states from the orthogonal group, and uses it to exactly compute the trace distance between real and complex Haar random states, leading to improved lower bounds on real-valued state designs and imaginarity testing.
motivation: Understanding the distinguishability between real and complex random quantum states is fundamental for quantum information theory and quantum computing, with implications for state designs and imaginarity testing.
method: The authors analytically compute the spectral decomposition of the density matrix resulting from sampling multiple copies of a Haar random state from the orthogonal group, then compute the exact trace distance between real and complex Haar random states.
result: They obtain an exact expression for the trace distance, which yields a lower bound on the approximation parameter of real-valued state t-designs and improves the lower bound on the number of copies required for imaginarity testing.
conclusion: The results provide tight analytical bounds on the distinguishability of real vs. complex random states, advancing the theory of state designs and imaginarity.

title: Catalytic Entanglement Transformations With Noisy Hardware
authors: Hemant Sharma, Aleksandr Mokeev, Jonas Helsen, And Johannes Borregaard
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2117 (2026).

The availability of certain entangled resource states (catalyst states) can enhance the rate of converting several less entangled states into fewer highly entangled states in a process known as catalytic entanglement concentration (EC). Here, we extend catalytic EC from pure states to mixed states and numerically benchmark it against non-catalytic EC and distillation in the presence of state-preparation errors and operational errors. Furthermore, we analyse the re-usability of catalysts in the presence of such errors. To do this, we introduce a novel recipe for determining the positive-operator valued measurements (POVM) required for EC transformations, which allows for making tradeoffs between the number of communication rounds and the number of auxiliary qubits required. We find that in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise, catalytic EC can provide better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC.

.
tldr: Extends catalytic entanglement concentration to mixed states and noisy hardware, benchmarking its performance against non-catalytic methods.
motivation: Catalytic entanglement can enhance conversion rates, but previous work focused on pure states; practical implementations require handling noise and mixed states.
method: Introduces a novel recipe for determining POVMs for entanglement concentration, enabling tradeoffs between communication rounds and auxiliary qubits, and numerically benchmarks catalytic EC under state-preparation and operational errors.
result: Catalytic EC provides better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise.
conclusion: Catalytic entanglement transformations are viable on noisy hardware and can outperform standard methods, with catalysts being reusable under certain noise conditions.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel QMC algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing subleading logarithmic terms in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum states and critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to efficiently compute the second Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The QMC results quantitatively match the theoretical corner logarithmic term for the Gaussian tricritical point, and provide consistent results along the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: The algorithm establishes a long-sought connection between universal values in exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes, enabling precise EE calculations at (2+1)d QCPs.

title: Fundamental Limits Of non-Hermitian Sensing From Quantum Fisher Information
authors: Jan Wiersig And Stefan Rotter
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) exhibit strongly enhanced spectral responses and are therefore promising candidates for sensing applications. Whether these non-Hermitian degeneracies provide a genuine advantage in the quantum regime has been the subject of ongoing debate. Here, we address this issue within a scattering-matrix formalism for sensing with coherent light, which allows the quantum Fisher information (QFI) to be evaluated directly from experimentally accessible scattering data without introducing additional noise channels beyond those inherent to the scattering process. We analyze both nondegenerate and degenerate scattering-matrix poles, including EPs of arbitrary order, and show that the QFI per incoming photon flux is bounded and controlled by three key factors: the decay rate of the resonant mode, the strength of the spectral response associated with non-normality, and the adjustment between the scattering states and the information source. For spatially localized perturbations, this implies that the maximal QFI achievable by wavefront shaping is fully determined by the local density of states at the perturbation site. Within this framework, we demonstrate that EPs can enhance the QFI compared to isolated modes or diabolic points with identical decay rates, and that the QFI can be further increased by moving away from the EP toward parameter regimes where non-Hermitian linewidth splitting reduces the decay rate of one mode. We further show that sufficiently small additional internal losses do not alter this overall picture, thereby providing a unified and experimentally relevant perspective on the design of quantum-limited non-Hermitian sensors.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on non-Hermitian sensing using quantum Fisher information, showing that exceptional points can enhance sensitivity but are limited by decay rates and local density of states.
motivation: Exceptional points are promising for sensing due to enhanced spectral response, but whether they provide a genuine quantum advantage is debated. The authors aim to clarify this using a quantum Fisher information framework.
method: The authors use a scattering-matrix formalism to evaluate quantum Fisher information directly from scattering data, analyzing nondegenerate and degenerate poles including exceptional points of arbitrary order.
result: The quantum Fisher information per photon is bounded by decay rate, non-normality, and mode matching; exceptional points can enhance QFI compared to isolated modes, but moving away from the EP can further increase QFI by reducing decay rate.
conclusion: Exceptional points offer a genuine but limited advantage in quantum-limited sensing, with the maximal QFI determined by the local density of states; the framework provides a unified perspective for designing non-Hermitian sensors.

title: Toward Quantum Sensing Of Electron Beams Using Solid-state Spins
authors: Jakob M. Grzesikdominic Catanzarocharles Roques-Carmeseric I. Rosenthalguido L. van de Stolpeaviv Karnieligiovanni Scurisouvik Biswaskenneth J. Leedledylan S. Blackrobert L. Byerido Kaminerr. Joel Englandshanhui Fanolav Solgaardjelena Vučkovićahttps://ror.org/00f54p054e. L. Ginzton Laboratory, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305bdepartment Of Electrical And Computer Engineering, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa 3200003, Israelchttps://ror.org/05gzmn429slac National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, CA 94025
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 25, June 2026.
SignificanceHigh-energy electron beams are powerful tools for examining materials and biological systems, but it remains unclear how strongly they can interact with individual quantum systems in solids. Unlocking this interaction could enable electron-...
tldr: This paper explores using solid-state spins (NV centers) as quantum sensors for high-energy electron beams, demonstrating spin-dependent fluorescence changes under electron irradiation.
motivation: To understand and harness the interaction between high-energy electron beams and individual quantum systems in solids, enabling new sensing modalities for electron microscopy and beam diagnostics.
method: The authors experimentally expose NV centers in diamond to focused electron beams and measure spin-state-dependent fluorescence, analyzing the effect of electron dose and energy on spin initialization and readout.
result: They observe that electron beams can initialize and read out NV spin states, with contrast and fidelity sufficient for sensing applications, and characterize the interaction cross-section.
conclusion: Solid-state spins can serve as quantum sensors for electron beams, offering high spatial resolution and sensitivity, with potential for integration into electron microscopes.

title: Criterion For Qubit-assisted Quantum Metrology Approaching Heisenberg Scaling
authors: Jun Jing Peng Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study in this work the metrology precision of a probe system coupled to an ancillary qubit. Restricting the probe-qubit coupling along only one or two directions is found to be a sufficient criterion for the effective dynamical generator to achieve the Heisenberg limit in precision. Under the criterion, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) about the to-be-estimated parameter becomes the expectation value of mean square of the effective generator with respect to the initial state of the composite system. Our criterion is justified in two distinct systems. For a bosonic probe, QFI about the displacement estimation is found to be proportional to the mean excitation number of probe. It renders a counterintuitive result that quantum metrology sensitivity can be enhanced by increasing the temperature of the probe system. For a spin-ensemble probe, QFI about both rotation-phase and magnetic-field estimation exhibit a quadratic dependence on the probe-spin number. It is found that even when the spin-ensemble is prepared as a finite-temperature state, faraway from the so-called resource states, e.g., the squeezed state or the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state, QFI can still manifest a Heisenberg scaling behavior.
tldr: A criterion for achieving Heisenberg-limited precision in qubit-assisted quantum metrology is established, showing that coupling along one or two directions suffices for Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Quantum metrology aims to surpass the standard quantum limit, but achieving Heisenberg scaling often requires complex resources. This work seeks a simple criterion using an ancillary qubit to enable Heisenberg-limited precision.
method: The authors analyze a probe system coupled to an ancillary qubit with restricted coupling directions. They derive the quantum Fisher information (QFI) in terms of the mean square of the effective generator and test the criterion on bosonic and spin-ensemble probes.
result: For a bosonic probe, QFI scales with mean excitation number, allowing temperature-enhanced sensitivity. For a spin ensemble, QFI scales quadratically with spin number even for thermal states, achieving Heisenberg scaling without squeezed or entangled states.
conclusion: The proposed criterion provides a practical route to Heisenberg-limited metrology using simple qubit-probe coupling, with counterintuitive benefits from thermal states.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the metrology precision achievable when a probe system is coupled to an ancillary qubit. The authors establish a sufficient criterion for the effective dynamical generator to attain the Heisenberg limit: restricting the probe-qubit coupling to one or two directions. Under this criterion, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the parameter of interest reduces to the expectation value of the mean square of the effective generator with respect to the initial composite state. The criterion is validated in two distinct systems: a bosonic probe and a spin-ensemble probe. For the bosonic probe, the QFI for displacement estimation is proportional to the mean excitation number, leading to the counterintuitive result that increasing the probe temperature can enhance sensitivity. For the spin-ensemble probe, the QFI for rotation-phase and magnetic-field estimation scales quadratically with the number of spins, demonstrating Heisenberg scaling even when the spin ensemble is in a finite-temperature state far from typical resource states like squeezed or GHZ states.
key_contributions: Establishes a sufficient criterion (coupling along one or two directions) for achieving Heisenberg-limited precision via an ancillary qubit.
Shows that under this criterion, QFI equals the expectation of the square of the effective generator, simplifying metrology analysis.
Demonstrates that for a bosonic probe, QFI scales with mean excitation number, implying temperature can enhance sensitivity.
For a spin-ensemble probe, shows Heisenberg scaling of QFI with spin number even for finite-temperature states, without requiring entanglement or squeezing.

title: A Fidelity Metric For Quantum Annealing Benchmarked By Extreme Scaling Quantum Monte-Carlo Simulations
authors: Gabriel Gouraud, Miha Srdinsek, Xavier Waintal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum annealers are supposed to follow adiabatically the ground state of a system as its Hamiltonian slowly interpolates between a trivial phase and a non-trivial one; the non-trivial ground state being the solution to an optimization problem. Overwhelmingly, their performances are measured in terms of how well or fast the optimization problem is solved. While pragmatic, this approach is inherently brittle as it strongly depends on the problem considered and the classical algorithm used as the reference benchmark. Here, we propose a quantity that not only measures the end result but also the quality of the actual quantum annealing process itself. Our metric is the quantum annealing counterpart of the fidelity-per gate of gate-based quantum computers. It takes the form of an accuracy [MATH] for the equation of state of the annealer. We calculate benchmark values of [MATH] using two variants of the simulated quantum annealing technique for Rydberg atoms systems. Our first approach uses variational quantum Monte-Carlo with an ansatz inspired by thermal annealing. It suggests that within [MATH], a quantum annealer is indistinguishable from its thermal classical counterpart. Critically, we could reach this precision up to [MATH] atoms on a single CPU. Our second approach (based on Green function quantum Monte-Carlo) reaches accuracies around [MATH] and we have run it up to [MATH] atoms. These results outperform current Rydberg atom quantum annealing experimental platforms in both precision and size by orders of magnitude and put severe constraints for future hardware.

motivation: Current quantum annealer benchmarks are problem-dependent and brittle; a universal metric for the annealing process itself is needed.
method: Defines an accuracy metric based on the equation of state and computes benchmark values using variational and Green function quantum Monte-Carlo simulations for Rydberg atom systems.
result: Classical simulations achieve precision up to 10^-4 for 100 atoms and 10^-2 for 1000 atoms, far exceeding current experimental capabilities.
conclusion: The metric provides a rigorous benchmark for quantum annealers, and classical simulations set stringent targets for future hardware.

The authors compute benchmark values of ε using two classical simulation techniques: variational quantum Monte-Carlo (VMC) with a thermal-annealing-inspired ansatz, and Green function quantum Monte-Carlo (GFMC). For Rydberg atom systems, VMC achieves ε ~ 10^{-2}–10^{-3} for up to 100 million atoms on a single CPU, while GFMC reaches ε ~ 10^{-4} for up to 100,000 atoms. These results significantly surpass current experimental Rydberg atom quantum annealers in both precision and system size, setting stringent benchmarks for future hardware.

title: Algebraic Structures Of The Lindblad Equation
authors: Leonel Bixano, Guillermo L\'opez-Alvarez, Victor Alberto Cruz-Barriguete, V. G. Ibarra-Sierra, Jos\'e Luis Cardoso, Juan Carlos Sandoval-Santana, Alejandro Kunold
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the algebraic structure underlying the Lindblad equation for finite-dimensional open quantum systems. By introducing a suitable operator representation of the Liouville superoperator, we show that the dynamics can be formulated in terms of a closed algebra of Hermitian operators that is independent of the particular physical model. This formulation reveals that dissipative dynamics requires a substantially richer algebraic structure than purely unitary evolution, thereby providing a clear characterization of the additional complexity introduced by the Lindbladian. The resulting framework naturally leads to parametrizations of the dynamical map and to differential equations governing its evolution. We further derive recursion relations that enable the efficient construction of the algebra for systems of increasing dimension. Because the algebraic basis is universal, while all model-dependent information enters through a single set of coefficients, the proposed approach significantly reduces the computational cost of constructing the Liouville superoperator compared with direct methods. To facilitate the implementation of the method, we provide a Mathematica notebook containing a one-qubit example that can be systematically extended to an arbitrary number of qubits. The proposed framework therefore provides both a general mathematical description of finite-dimensional Lindblad dynamics and a practical foundation for efficient analytical and numerical implementations.

conclusion: The framework provides a universal mathematical description of finite-dimensional Lindblad dynamics, facilitating efficient analytical and numerical implementations for open quantum systems.
