[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: Reducing T-count is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based circuits.
result: The relation enables significant T-count reduction compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a new tool for optimizing fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide a framework to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and quantify how interactions affect their non-Abelian properties.
conclusion: The work establishes practical measures for identifying Majorana bound states in realistic interacting systems, guiding experimental efforts toward topological qubits.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, enabling analysis of error thresholds and resource requirements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for evaluating magic state preparation protocols, which is important for the development of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion processes.
result: They show how these methods provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions, fluctuation spectra, and large deviations.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems for novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators enables rich nonequilibrium phenomena with potential for ultrafast control of material properties.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. Temporal coarse-graining is then achieved by conditioning the stochastic process on a coarse realization of the noise, expressing the conditioned stochastic process in terms of a sum of smooth, deterministic functions and bridge processes with boundaries fixed at zero, and performing the ensemble average over the bridge processes. For Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, the deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the stochastic bridge processes are not only independent but taken from the same distribution with correlators that can be expressed analytically, allowing the associated noise propagators to be precomputed once for all simulations. This combination of noise trajectories on a coarse time grid and ensemble averaging over bridge processes has practical advantages, such as a simple concatenation rule, that we highlight with numerical examples.

.
tldr: A method for simulating quantum systems with classical stochastic noise using temporal coarse-graining and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems with noise that has temporal correlations over many time scales (e.g., 1/f noise) is computationally challenging.
method: The noise is expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes; temporal coarse-graining is achieved by conditioning on a coarse realization and analytically averaging over bridge processes.
result: The deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and bridge processes are independent with analytically known correlators, enabling precomputation of noise propagators.
conclusion: The approach provides practical advantages like a simple concatenation rule and is demonstrated with numerical examples.

title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: Derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical circuits that provide necessary conditions for exact and approximate state preparation.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of linear optical state preparation is crucial for generating entangled resources like NOON states without post-selection.
method: Maps the evolution of quantum states under passive linear interferometers onto the Lie algebra of the corresponding Hamiltonians and identifies conserved quantities (e.g., spectrum of the density matrix).
result: Provides invariants that must match for exact state preparation and a lower bound on the distance to a target state based on invariant mismatch.
conclusion: These invariants can be used to rule out impossible linear optical evolutions, guiding future state preparation methods.

title: Thermomechanics Of Odd Matter: From Deterministic To Stochastic Media
authors: Martin Ostoja-Starzewski
abstract: Odd matter exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive response while remaining compatible with balance laws and the second law of thermodynamics. We develop a unified continuum framework based on Edelen’s primitive thermodynamics, which decomposes generalized forces into gradient (hyperdissipative) and orthogonal (powerless) components. We show that this convex decomposition in velocity space admits an elastic analogue: hyperelastic response corresponds to integrable stresses derived from a stored-energy potential, while odd elasticity arises as the non-integrable, yet not derivable from a stored-energy potential branch of admissible response. Within the odd elasticity, we distinguish two cases: an instantaneous power orthogonality (the stronger one) or a configurational orthogonality (the weaker one). Working within the case of configurational orthogonality we construct the (linear) thermo-poromechanical theory, derive a finite strain odd neo-Hookean solid, and establish preservation of coercivity and exponential energy decay in random fluid and solid odd continua. Scale-dependent homogenization preserves coercivity of the even part and orthogonality of the odd part. In driven granular Couette flow, odd stresses modify fluctuation statistics without producing entropy, consistent with the fluctuation theorem. The results provide a systematic thermodynamic foundation for odd matter in deterministic and stochastic settings.
tldr: Develops a thermodynamic framework for odd matter using Edelen's primitive thermodynamics, showing odd elasticity as non-integrable but admissible response.
motivation: Odd matter exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive response, and a unified thermodynamic foundation is needed to reconcile it with balance laws and the second law.
method: Uses convex decomposition of generalized forces into gradient and orthogonal components, and constructs linear thermo-poromechanical theory and finite strain odd neo-Hookean solid.
result: Establishes preservation of coercivity and exponential energy decay in random odd continua; odd stresses in granular Couette flow modify fluctuation statistics without entropy production.
conclusion: Provides a systematic thermodynamic basis for odd matter, linking odd elasticity to non-integrable response while respecting thermodynamics.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: Demonstrates Kovacs-type memory effects in nanoparticle orientational relaxation and designs protocols to accelerate dynamics by suppressing slow modes.
motivation: Understanding and overcoming memory effects that limit acceleration of relaxation in stochastic systems with many degrees of freedom.
method: Optical birefringence measurements of field-induced orientation in polydisperse nanoparticle suspensions, analyzed via Smoluchowski equation and multiscale relaxation theory.
result: Kovacs nonmonotonic relaxation observed; memory arises from polydispersity; sequential suppression of slow modes reduces relaxation time significantly.
conclusion: Memory effects in multiscale stochastic dynamics can be mitigated by tailored control protocols, offering a strategy for accelerating relaxation.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, enabling universal quantum computing with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is a key challenge for universal quantum computing, especially on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that achieve fault tolerance for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, using a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and compatible with planar chips, demonstrating a practical path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: Twisted color circuits provide a viable approach for implementing non-Clifford gates fault-tolerantly on the 2D color code, advancing toward scalable quantum computers.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: Proves that wide quantum neural networks with Clifford+Pauli gates cannot achieve quantum advantage by showing their neural tangent kernel can be computed classically.
motivation: To determine whether quantum neural networks can provide a quantum advantage over classical models, specifically by analyzing their training dynamics via the neural tangent kernel.
method: Replaces the average over initialization parameters in the NTK with an average over four discrete Clifford values, enabling efficient classical simulation of the circuit.
result: The NTK of such quantum neural networks can be computed classically in polynomial time, implying that wide networks are equivalent to Gaussian processes and thus classically simulable.
conclusion: Wide quantum neural networks of the considered class cannot achieve quantum advantage, as their expected output can be computed classically.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump
authors: Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Guanjun Zeng, Xiaozhou Pan, Kai Zhang, and Jietai Jing

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hexapartite active nonlinear feedback control system using two four-wave-mixing processes with a spatially structured pump for manipulating nonclassical beams.
motivation: Feedback control is important for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams in quantum information science, and the authors aim to extend this to a hexapartite system.
method: The authors theoretically design a system with two four-wave-mixing processes and a spatially structured pump to achieve active nonlinear feedback control.
result: The system generates hexapartite entangled states and allows control over the entanglement structure.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a method for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement, which may be useful for quantum information processing.

title: Non-Hermitian Bloch Oscillations
authors: Tomoki Ozawa Yanyan He
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a general framework for non-Hermitian Bloch oscillations by investigating the wave-packet dynamics in one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices driven by a dc force. The equations of motion for the momentum, center of mass, and group velocity of a wave packet are derived, where an anomalous group velocity due to the non-Hermiticity is identified. We show that nonreciprocal non-smooth Bloch oscillations, characterized by periodic jumps in group velocity, can emerge, and we analyze the role of finite-size effects. In non-Hermitian lattices with unidirectional hopping under open boundary conditions, we further uncover the emergence of periodic temporal Goos--H\"anchen shifts together with an anomalous wave propagation along the direction of vanishing hopping.
tldr: This paper studies non-Hermitian Bloch oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, deriving equations of motion and uncovering anomalous group velocity and periodic Goos-Hänchen shifts.
motivation: To understand wave-packet dynamics in non-Hermitian systems under a dc force, which is a fundamental problem in non-Hermitian physics.
method: The authors derive equations of motion for momentum, center of mass, and group velocity using a semiclassical approach, and analyze finite-size effects and open boundary conditions.
result: They identify nonreciprocal non-smooth Bloch oscillations with periodic jumps in group velocity, and for unidirectional hopping, periodic temporal Goos-Hänchen shifts with anomalous wave propagation.
conclusion: The work establishes a general framework for non-Hermitian Bloch oscillations, revealing novel dynamical phenomena absent in Hermitian systems.

title: Shallow Quantum Circuits For Deep Chemistry Via Valence Bond Embeddings
authors: Jakob S. Kottmann Francisco Javier Del Arco Santos
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum chemistry is one of the major potential applications in quantum computation. Currently there is a considerable focus on relatively small active spaces as a consequence of hardware noise and exponential bottlenecks in simulations. In the long run, there will be an increasing demand in reliable approximations for larger systems -- both, as initial states for projective algorithms like the quantum phase estimation or for the evaluation of dynamical properties. While numerous approaches to select active spaces and extrapolate basis set accuracy exist, there is currently no consistent approach that results in a single quantum circuit for the total system. In this work, we combine hybrid Fermionic-Bosonic encodings with the structured approach of Quantum Valence Bond Theory to directly construct quantum circuits for comparably large molecular systems. With this approach we are able to push simulability barrier of variational quantum eigensolvers towards chemically relevant systems and demonstrate circuit designs that outperform active space counterparts and achieve good approximations with respect to the exact solutions.
tldr: Combines hybrid Fermionic-Bosonic encodings with Quantum Valence Bond Theory to construct quantum circuits for large molecular systems, pushing the simulability barrier of variational quantum eigensolvers.
motivation: Quantum chemistry is a key application for quantum computing, but current approaches are limited to small active spaces due to hardware noise and exponential bottlenecks. There is a need for reliable approximations for larger systems.
method: The authors use hybrid Fermionic-Bosonic encodings and the structured approach of Quantum Valence Bond Theory to directly construct quantum circuits for large molecular systems, avoiding the need for active space selection.
result: The circuit designs outperform active space counterparts and achieve good approximations to exact solutions for chemically relevant systems.
conclusion: This approach enables variational quantum eigensolvers to handle larger molecular systems, potentially advancing quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices.

title: Quantum Statistics On Atom-ion Feshbach Resonances
authors: Joachim Siemund, Fabian Thielemann, Jonathan Grieshaber, Wei Wu, Patrick Mullan, Panagiotis Giannakeas, Krzysztof Jachymski, Tobias Schaetz
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate three-body recombination in a hybrid atom-ion system consisting of a single trapped Ba[MATH] ion immersed in a two-component Fermi gas of Li atoms near an atom-ion Feshbach resonance. By tuning the spin composition at constant density and temperature, we isolate the role of quantum statistics in atom-atom-ion collisions. The measured ion loss rate exhibits a pronounced nonlinear dependence on spin polarization, revealing a reduced contribution of recombination pathways involving identical fermions already at the level of experimental observables. The observations are consistent with a two-step recombination picture and an adiabatic hyperspherical approach, where antisymmetrization restricts the available entrance channels and gives rise to interference between indistinguishable recombination pathways. Our work establishes atom-ion systems as a platform for controlling three-body collisions via quantum statistics and demonstrates that exchange-symmetry effects remain robust even under thermal averaging that obscures the underlying threshold-law behavior.
tldr: This paper studies three-body recombination in a hybrid atom-ion system, focusing on the role of quantum statistics in collisions near a Feshbach resonance.
motivation: Understanding how quantum statistics affects three-body collisions in hybrid atom-ion systems is important for controlling such systems, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.
method: The authors measure ion loss rates in a Ba+ ion immersed in a two-component Fermi gas of Li atoms, varying spin polarization, and compare with a two-step recombination model and adiabatic hyperspherical approach.
result: The ion loss rate shows a nonlinear dependence on spin polarization, indicating reduced recombination involving identical fermions due to antisymmetrization and interference.
conclusion: Atom-ion systems can be used to control three-body collisions via quantum statistics, but the work is primarily about atomic physics and ultracold collisions, not the user's focus areas.

title: MPE-Adam: Multi-Population Evolutionary Optimization With Adam Refinement For Qaoa
authors: Chi Quan Luu, Thai T. Vu, John Le
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parameter optimization is a central bottleneck in variational quantum algorithms such as the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The classical optimizer must navigate a high-dimensional, non-convex parameter space under measurement noise. From a quantum software perspective, this process forms a multi-stage workflow: global exploration of the parameter space followed by local refinement within the hybrid quantum-classical loop. Most existing approaches, however, employ single-stage optimizers that do not separate these roles, which limits the use of complementary strategies. We propose MPE-Adam, a hybrid optimization framework that integrates multi-population evolutionary search for global exploration with Adam-based gradient refinement for local convergence. The method is structured as a modular component suitable for quantum software pipelines. We evaluate MPE-Adam on MaxCut instances generated from random 3-regular graphs with up to 22 nodes. The results show that MPE-Adam achieves higher approximation ratios and lower variance than evolutionary-only and SPSA-based baselines, with statistically significant improvements. These findings indicate that structured multi-stage optimization improves both solution quality and software-level flexibility in quantum applications.
tldr: MPE-Adam is a hybrid optimization framework combining multi-population evolutionary search with Adam refinement for QAOA parameter optimization.
motivation: Parameter optimization in variational quantum algorithms like QAOA is challenging due to high-dimensional, non-convex landscapes and measurement noise; existing single-stage optimizers lack complementary exploration and refinement strategies.
method: The framework uses multi-population evolutionary search for global exploration and then applies Adam-based gradient refinement for local convergence, structured as a modular component for quantum software pipelines.
result: On MaxCut instances from random 3-regular graphs up to 22 nodes, MPE-Adam achieves higher approximation ratios and lower variance than evolutionary-only and SPSA-based baselines with statistical significance.
conclusion: Structured multi-stage optimization improves solution quality and software flexibility in quantum applications, but the paper focuses on classical optimization heuristics rather than fundamental quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Real-Space Topology And Charge Order In The Haldane-Holstein Model
authors: Sebastião Dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, And Rubem Mondaini
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastião dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, and Rubem Mondaini

We study the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model, where a paradigmatic Chern insulator is coupled to fully dynamical phonons, and provide an unbiased characterization of how retarded electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology. Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo, we find that increasin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Haldane-Holstein model, focusing on how electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology and induce charge order, using determinant quantum Monte Carlo.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topological order and electron-phonon coupling in a Chern insulator, which is relevant for condensed matter physics but not directly tied to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model with dynamical phonons.
result: Increasing electron-phonon coupling leads to a transition from a Chern insulator to a charge-ordered state, destroying the topological phase.
conclusion: Retarded electron-phonon interactions can destabilize Chern topology, highlighting the fragility of topological phases in the presence of strong coupling to phonons.

title: Increasing The Stability Of A Superfluid In A Rotating Necklace Potential
authors: Giulio Nesti And Luca Pezzè
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Nesti and Luca Pezzè

Recent experiments have probed the stability of ring superfluids in the presence of Josephson barriers or Gaussian impurities. Here we present a theoretical analysis that extends beyond the regimes explored so far. We study the onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid, addressing both t…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063326] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential, focusing on stability beyond previous experimental regimes.
motivation: Recent experiments probed ring superfluid stability with barriers; this work extends the theoretical analysis to new parameter regimes.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field and Bogoliubov methods to study onset of dynamical instabilities in a ring superfluid with a rotating necklace potential.
result: Identifies conditions for increased stability and characterizes instability thresholds as a function of potential strength and rotation speed.
conclusion: The rotating necklace potential can enhance superfluid stability under certain conditions, relevant for ultracold atom experiments.

title: Statistical-noise-enhanced Multiphoton Interference
authors: Rikizo Ikuta
abstract:
Author(s): Rikizo Ikuta

Photon statistics plays a governing role in multiphoton interference. While interference visibility in the standard two-photon case, known as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, monotonically degrades with higher intensity correlation functions, we show that this monotonicity does not hold for three-photon…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063731] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that statistical noise can enhance multiphoton interference visibility beyond the monotonic degradation expected from standard two-photon interference.
motivation: To understand how higher-order intensity correlations affect multiphoton interference, specifically whether the monotonic degradation seen in two-photon Hong-Ou-Mandel interference extends to three-photon cases.
method: Theoretical analysis of multiphoton interference with statistical noise, using correlation functions and quantum optics formalism.
result: For three-photon interference, the visibility does not monotonically degrade with higher-order correlations; statistical noise can actually enhance interference.
conclusion: Statistical noise can be beneficial in multiphoton interference, challenging the conventional wisdom that noise always degrades quantum interference.

title: Triggering And Switching Of Topological Phases And non-Hermitian Transitions In A Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Circuit With Long-range Hopping And Synthetic Gauge Fields
authors: Jing Cheng, Cheng-Jun Han, Jin-Yan Hu, Mo-Nan Wang, And Y. P. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Cheng, Cheng-Jun Han, Jin-Yan Hu, Mo-Nan Wang, and Y. P. Wang

We propose an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain that integrates long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, providing a tunable circuit platform to trigger and control non-Hermitian transitions and topological phase transitions. We show that the long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063732] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions and non-Hermitian transitions in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger circuit with long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields.
motivation: To understand how long-range hopping and synthetic gauge fields can trigger and control topological and non-Hermitian transitions in a tunable circuit platform.
method: The authors propose an extended SSH chain model with long-range hopping and a synthetic Peierls phase, and analyze its topological phases and non-Hermitian transitions using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They show that long-range hopping strength acts as a trigger for topological phase transitions, and synthetic gauge fields enable switching between different topological phases.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for controlling topological and non-Hermitian phenomena, with potential applications in topological photonics and quantum simulation.

title: Theory Of Anomalous Landau-Zener Tunneling Induced By Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Wen-Yuan Wang And Hong-Juan Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Yuan Wang and Hong-Juan Meng

We develop a general theory of Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent, sign-reversible nonlinear coupling, distinguishing it fundamentally from conventional on-site nonlinearity. Through a combination of analytical and phase-space analysis, we show that beyond a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062218] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling.
motivation: To understand the effect of nonlinear coupling on Landau-Zener tunneling, which differs from conventional on-site nonlinearity.
method: Combines analytical and phase-space analysis to study the two-level system.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling, anomalous tunneling behavior emerges.
conclusion: The work provides a general theory for nonlinear Landau-Zener tunneling with sign-reversible coupling.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich
abstract:
Author(s): Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, and Luca Salasnich

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes the complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, proving that approximate sampling is hard for classical computers under standard assumptions.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs assumed a dilute regime where the number of photons is much smaller than the number of modes, but experimental demonstrations operate in the saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with modes. This gap needed to be bridged to justify quantum advantage claims in current experiments.
method: The authors develop new techniques based on the permanent-of-Gaussians conjecture and anticoncentration properties to prove that approximate BosonSampling in the saturated regime is #P-hard, using reductions from random circuit sampling and worst-case to average-case reductions.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is classically hard to simulate approximately, assuming the permanent-of-Gaussians conjecture and the non-collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. This provides rigorous complexity-theoretic support for near-term photonic quantum advantage experiments.
conclusion: The work validates that current photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime are indeed demonstrating a quantum computational advantage, and it opens the door to more efficient BosonSampling implementations.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the paper aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and connecting to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems through the lens of space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful analogy with quantum computation that simplifies the study of many-body dynamics.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has an irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that preserve a symmetry, which is a topic in quantum computation theory.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define two topological invariants: an anyon permutation map and a generalized GNVW index, and proves classification up to finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs for finite Abelian group symmetries, and demonstrates that the Kramers-Wannier duality cannot be extended to a full QCA.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous classification of symmetric QCAs, but is primarily a mathematical result in quantum cellular automata theory, not directly aligned with the user's core interests.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement in lossy multi-path atom interferometers using spin-squeezed states, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but is degraded by losses and finite temperature.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses from velocity selectivity and scattering, and one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree yields several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite realistic losses.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic conditions, but finite temperature poses a significant challenge.

title: Bosonic Content Of Three-fermion Highest-spin States
authors: Jerzy Cioslowski, Krzysztof Strasburger, And Denis K. Sunko
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2121 (2026).

A rigorous characterization of the information content of any highest-spin three-fermion wave function is presented. It is based upon a formal decomposition of the wave function into a finite set of fixed invariants, called shapes, whose sole purpose is to satisfy the Pauli principle, and a variable part, constituting the bosonic excitations of these invariants, that provides its physical content. As an example, this decomposition is applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of the lowest-energy quartet electronic state of the lithium atom. This wave function, which comprises hundreds of basis functions, is reduced to eleven shape blocks, only five of which are numerically significant. Such a compact characterization is a generic example of the appearance of superselection rules in configuration space, and provides a qualitative aid in the search for robust few-particle entangled states.

.
tldr: This paper decomposes three-fermion highest-spin wave functions into shape invariants and bosonic excitations, applied to the lithium atom.
motivation: To characterize the information content of fermionic wave functions and identify robust few-particle entangled states.
method: Formal decomposition of the wave function into fixed invariants (shapes) satisfying the Pauli principle and a variable bosonic part.
result: A benchmark lithium wave function with hundreds of basis functions is reduced to eleven shape blocks, five of which are numerically significant.
conclusion: The decomposition reveals superselection rules in configuration space and aids in finding robust entangled states.

title: A Survey Of Quantum Programming Languages
authors: Quan Do, Hersh Gupta, Xiyuan Cao, Aarav Pabla, Pranav Singamsetty, Evan O'grady, Keli Huang, Jens Palsberg
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing has seen multiple recent breakthroughs and is getting closer to demonstrations of an exponential advantage over classical computing for certain problems. Programmers will require high-level, general-purpose, executable programming languages to express quantum solutions clearly and effectively, and the field has already produced a wide variety of such languages. This paper presents a language classification framework and uses it to survey ten popular quantum programming languages. The findings include conceptual and experimental comparisons that result in a list of challenges for future language design.
tldr: A survey of ten quantum programming languages, comparing their features and challenges.
motivation: As quantum computing advances, programmers need high-level languages to express quantum algorithms; this survey aims to classify and compare existing languages.
method: The authors propose a language classification framework and apply it to analyze ten popular quantum programming languages conceptually and experimentally.
result: The survey provides a structured comparison and identifies challenges for future language design.
conclusion: Quantum programming languages are diverse and still evolving; future work should address the identified challenges.

title: Mechanisms Governing Photon-pair Generation And Emission Directionality In Quantum Metasurfaces
authors: Alberto Paniate, Ivano Ruo-Berchera, Francesco Monticone
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metasurfaces are emerging as a promising platform for photon-pair generation through spontaneous parametric down-conversion, thanks to their compactness, integrability, and intrinsic multifunctionality, which enables the engineering of complex quantum states. However, their full potential remains only partially exploited because the physical mechanisms governing key properties of the generated photon pairs, such as generation efficiency and emission directionality, are not yet fully understood. As a result, metasurface designs and experimental configurations are often optimized through trial-and-error procedures. Here, we theoretically investigate the main mechanisms that control photon-pair generation and detection by studying how different pump configurations and measurement geometries affect the generation efficiency, emission directionality, and collection efficiency of the emitted photon pairs. This framework allows us to interpret existing experimental results and to provide general guidelines for the design of metasurfaces and the choice of experimental configurations in future experiments. Finally, we show that substrate thickness and multilayer configurations represent additional degrees of freedom for quantum metasurface design and can be engineered to enhance the generation efficiency and control the emission directionality, providing a new route for the optimization of photon-pair sources based on metasurfaces.
tldr: The paper investigates mechanisms governing photon-pair generation and emission directionality in quantum metasurfaces for spontaneous parametric down-conversion.
motivation: To understand the physical mechanisms behind photon-pair generation efficiency and emission directionality in metasurfaces, which are currently optimized through trial-and-error.
method: Theoretical analysis of how pump configurations and measurement geometries affect generation efficiency, emission directionality, and collection efficiency.
result: Identifies key mechanisms and shows that substrate thickness and multilayer configurations can enhance generation efficiency and control emission directionality.
conclusion: Provides guidelines for designing metasurfaces and experimental configurations for optimized photon-pair sources.

title: Tailor Made Embeddings For Quantum Machine Learning
authors: Dominik \v{s}afr\'anek Aldo Lamarre
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoencoders transformed classical machine learning by solving the curse of dimensionality, enabling principled weight initialization and learning compact, structured representations. In this work, we extend this paradigm to quantum machine learning by introducing a variational autoencoder framework that learns task-specific quantum embeddings of classical data. We demonstrate that high-dimensional datasets, including ImageNet, can be compressed into a 13-qubit quantum representation while remaining reconstructable through a learned decoder. On MNIST (3 vs 5), our approach achieves 98.5% validation accuracy using a circuit-centric quantum classifier, within 1.2 percentage points of a classical neural network baseline (99.7%) and more than 30 percentage points above a naive amplitude-embedding approach. Unlike amplitude embeddings, which require full quantum state tomography for recovery, or angle embeddings, which generally rely on circuit inversion under restrictive assumptions, the proposed framework reconstructs the original data from only a polynomial number of measurements. The framework was further validated on IBM quantum hardware, confirming that the learned embeddings remain stable and reconstructable under real device noise.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational autoencoder framework for learning task-specific quantum embeddings of classical data, achieving high compression and reconstruction on quantum hardware.
motivation: Classical autoencoders solve the curse of dimensionality and learn compact representations; this work extends that paradigm to quantum machine learning to enable efficient quantum embeddings.
method: A variational autoencoder is used to learn a quantum embedding of classical data into a 13-qubit state, with a learned decoder for reconstruction from polynomial measurements.
result: On MNIST (3 vs 5), the approach achieves 98.5% validation accuracy, within 1.2% of a classical baseline, and outperforms naive amplitude embedding by >30%. Embeddings remain stable under IBM quantum hardware noise.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical method for compressing classical data into quantum states suitable for quantum machine learning, with demonstrated hardware feasibility.

title: Weak-Strong Resurgence Duality
authors: Ayssar I. Farah Gerald V. Dunne
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there is an explicit resurgent duality between weak and strong coupling expansions when one of the expansions has zero radius of convergence and the other has infinite radius of convergence. This complements the situation where the convergent expansion has finite radius of convergence, or when both expansions have zero radius of convergence. We illustrate this phenomenon for the Airy and Pearcey catastrophe integrals, and we apply it to two physical examples: the weak and strong coupling expansions of Dyson-Schwinger equations in zero-dimensional scalar [MATH] theories, and the short and long time expansions of the heat kernel trace for the fluctuation operator of the kink-antikink crystal saddle configuration in the Gross-Neveu model.
tldr: The paper establishes a resurgent duality between weak and strong coupling expansions in quantum field theory and related integrals.
motivation: To understand the relationship between perturbative and non-perturbative expansions when one has zero radius of convergence and the other infinite.
method: Uses resurgence theory and analyzes Airy and Pearcey integrals, then applies to Dyson-Schwinger equations and heat kernel traces.
result: Demonstrates explicit duality between weak and strong coupling expansions in several examples.
conclusion: Resurgent duality provides a new perspective on non-perturbative physics and connects seemingly different expansion regimes.

title: Taming The Single-cylinder Scattering Through Time-modulation -- The Role Of The Modulation Phase
authors: J. Yan, I. Katsantonis, M. Mostafa, V. Asadchy, M. Kafesaki
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dielectric particles with time-modulated electromagnetic properties exhibit intriguing scattering phenomena, entailing unique response and possibilities in meta-structures made of such particles. In this work, we investigate the scattering properties of an infinitely-long cylinder with periodically time-modulated permittivity. We demonstrate parametric scattering amplification, depending on the strength of the modulation, as well as controllable angular scattering pattern, ranging from enhanced forward to enhanced backward, or even scattering cancellation. This angular tunability is achieved through appropriate control of the modulation phase, highlighting its critical role in multi-modal time-modulated scattering systems.
tldr: This paper studies time-modulated dielectric cylinders for controlling scattering patterns via modulation phase.
motivation: To achieve tunable scattering properties in meta-structures using time-varying materials.
method: Analytical and numerical investigation of an infinitely-long cylinder with periodically time-modulated permittivity.
result: Demonstrates parametric scattering amplification and angular pattern control (forward, backward, cancellation) by adjusting modulation phase.
conclusion: The modulation phase is a critical parameter for multi-modal scattering control in time-modulated systems.

title: Scalable Message-Passing Quantum Graph Neural Networks In The Weisfeiler-Leman Hierarchy
authors: Snehal Raj, Brian Coyle, L\'eo Monbroussou, Andr\'e J. Ferreira-Martins, Renato M. S. Farias, Elham Kashefi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graphs provide a natural language for relational data in chemistry, biology and optimisation. Graph neural networks (GNNs) have driven much of the recent progress in learning from such data through message passing, a single primitive that generalises convolution and attention. Quantum counterparts have been proposed, but with limited connection to message passing and few guarantees on performance or scalability. More broadly, the trainability of variational quantum circuits is a recognised bottleneck for their wide applicability, and pre-training has emerged as one way to address it. Yet for a quantum model to be useful, it must offer expressivity guarantees along with demonstrable scalability. Here we show how a quantum graph neural network can be built to perform message passing, to be permutation equivariant, and to sit at a chosen level of the Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy, the standard measure of how finely a model can tell graphs apart. We show that, as for classical GNNs, the training can be done first on small graph instances, allowing for a pre-training that can mitigate usual training issues, and its output can be read out at a cost that stays low as the graph grows. We validate the framework in large-scale simulations of up to 56 qubits across three datasets, on synthetic graphs that ordinary message passing cannot separate, on molecular property prediction, and on the travelling salesperson problem. Our framework opens a path for near-term quantum algorithms with theoretical guarantees and practical scalability, bringing the principles of graph learning into quantum circuit design.
tldr: A quantum graph neural network framework that implements message passing with Weisfeiler-Lehman expressivity guarantees and demonstrates scalability up to 56 qubits.
motivation: Classical GNNs are powerful but quantum counterparts lack rigorous connection to message passing and scalability guarantees; the paper aims to bridge this gap.
method: The authors design a permutation-equivariant quantum circuit that performs message passing on graphs, with expressivity controlled by the Weisfeiler-Lehman hierarchy, and use pre-training on small graphs to mitigate training issues.
result: The framework is validated on synthetic graphs, molecular property prediction, and the travelling salesperson problem using simulations up to 56 qubits, showing that pre-training improves trainability and that readout cost remains low as graph size grows.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable quantum GNN with theoretical expressivity guarantees, opening a path for near-term quantum algorithms in graph learning.

title: Unified Nilpotent Operational Framework: Foundations, Algebraic Exactness, And Complexity
authors: Ramon Moya
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A unified algebraic framework is developed to study nilpotency as a structural mechanism for exactness in operational, combinatorial, and computational problems. The central object is the Nilpotent Operational System (SON), formalized as a tuple (R, N, m, M_R), where R is a C-algebra, N satisfies N^{m+1}=0, and M_R(m) is the arithmetic cost of a product in R. The basic result is the Exact Termination Lemma: every formal series evaluated at N collapses to an exact finite sum of m+1 terms. Three complexity regimes are obtained: truncated series (quasi-linear bound via Newton iteration), nilpotent operators (linear bound via Horner evaluation), and incidence algebras (quasi-quadratic bound). Applications include classical and free cumulants, Appell sequences, orthogonal polynomials, Stirling numbers, M\"obius inversion, Witt vectors, and local holonomic functions. In all cases except Stirling numbers, strict complexity improvements over classical algorithms are obtained. For classical cumulants, equivalence with polynomial multiplication is achieved: L(C_n)=Theta(M(n)). For free cumulants, the complete equivalence T_{FC}(n)=Theta(M(n)) is established via the Voiculescu functional equation and compositional reversal.
tldr: Develops a unified algebraic framework for nilpotent structures with applications to combinatorial and computational problems, but lacks connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To provide a general algebraic framework for exactness in operational and combinatorial problems using nilpotency.
method: Formalizes a Nilpotent Operational System (SON) and proves the Exact Termination Lemma; applies to cumulants, orthogonal polynomials, and other combinatorial objects.
result: Derives complexity bounds for truncated series, nilpotent operators, and incidence algebras, achieving strict improvements over classical algorithms for most cases.
conclusion: The framework unifies many combinatorial and algebraic structures under nilpotency, offering efficient algorithms, but does not address quantum or thermodynamic systems.

title: Grouped Reverse Importance Sampling For The Partition Function
authors: Neri Merhav
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and analyze several grouped variants of the method of reverse importance sampling (RIS) for estimating a partition function from samples of the Boltzmann distribution [MATH]. Ordinary RIS weighs each sample separately. By contrast, our proposed grouped RIS (GRIS) methods are based on assigning the samples into groups (or batches) of size [MATH] and applying a joint weight function to each group. The focal point of the research is the quest for a tractable weight function that would yield the smallest possible mean squared error (MSE). A simple identity relates the normalized MSE to the chi-squared divergence between the joint-weight distribution and the distribution of the [MATH]-fold sum of independent energies. Our first theoretical finding is that any weight that improves on ordinary RIS ([MATH]) must couple the group components. In other words, it must not be a product-form function across those components, as product-form weight functions always worsen the MSE. Our second, and more important, finding is that, without loss of optimality, it is sufficient to seek weight functions that depend only on the total energy, [MATH], of the group (group-energy weight functions); for the sliding-window variants, the analogous result is open. This finding simplifies both the theoretical analysis and the application of the method substantially. For [MATH] and [MATH], the MSE associated with non-overlapping (NOL) groups is reduced by [MATH]--[MATH] across three examples. We then propose two additional variants of GRIS, both based on sliding-window grouping (as opposed to NOL grouping). The first applies a fixed weight sliding window (FSW) across all (cyclic) shifts of the sliding window, and the second allows a variable-weight sliding window (VSW). The FSW scheme improves on the NOL one, and the VSW improves even further, as will be demonstrated numerically.
tldr: This paper introduces grouped reverse importance sampling methods for estimating partition functions, focusing on minimizing mean squared error through joint weight functions.
motivation: Estimating partition functions is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and machine learning, and improving the efficiency of sampling-based methods is of broad interest.
method: The authors propose grouped reverse importance sampling (GRIS) variants that assign samples into groups and apply joint weight functions, analyzing non-overlapping and sliding-window grouping schemes.
result: They prove that optimal weight functions depend only on the total energy of the group, and demonstrate MSE reductions of 30-50% for small group sizes in examples.
conclusion: Grouped RIS with energy-based weight functions can significantly improve estimation accuracy, with sliding-window variants offering further gains.

title: An Information-Theoretic Metric For Semantic Value Of Spatiotemporal Information
authors: Zijing Wang, Zhijin Qin, Siyu Lin, Wei Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the explosive growth of network scale and data volume, wireless communication is facing an increasingly severe limitation of spectrum resources. Semantic communication has emerged as a promising paradigm to break the bandwidth bottleneck by transmitting significant task-oriented semantic information rather than raw data. In practical real-time wireless applications, semantics of information exhibit diverse spatial and temporal correlations depending on intrinsic dynamics of source and extrinsic dynamics of environment. Motivated by this observation, this paper develops a novel information-theoretic metric to quantify the semantic value of spatiotemporal information. Specifically, a semantic value of information (SVoI) framework is proposed based on the mutual information, which characterises the reduction in uncertainty when predicting an unknown system state using past semantic spatiotemporal correlated observations. Focusing on general Gaussian Markov models, closed-form expressions of the SVoI are derived. Effects of both separable and coupled spatiotemporal correlations on SVoI are further investigated analytically. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the theoretical analysis of SVoI and its bounds. The proposed SVoI metric jointly captures the impact of semantic spatiotemporal correlation of source, timeliness of information, and channel conditions, which could serve as an effective optimisation objective for the design of next-generation semantic-aware communication systems.
tldr: The paper proposes a semantic value of information metric based on mutual information for spatiotemporal data in wireless communication.
motivation: To address spectrum scarcity in wireless networks by enabling semantic communication that transmits only task-relevant information.
method: Develops a semantic value of information (SVoI) framework using mutual information to quantify uncertainty reduction from past observations, with closed-form expressions for Gaussian Markov models.
result: Derives analytical expressions for SVoI under separable and coupled spatiotemporal correlations, validated by simulations.
conclusion: The SVoI metric captures spatiotemporal correlation, timeliness, and channel conditions, serving as an optimization objective for semantic-aware communication systems.

title: Construction Of Lyapunov Density For Nonautonomous Dynamical Systems On Hypertorus
authors: \"ozkan Karabacak Swapnil Tripathi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a semidefinite programming framework for constructing time-varying Lyapunov densities for nonautonomous dynamical systems on a hypertorus. The formulation leverages Gram matrix representations of hybrid (real-trigonometric) polynomials. In addition, we introduce a novel block decomposition of these Gram representations to confine the blow-up of the resulting density to a prescribed set. The results are then applied to establish the almost global synchronization of a time-varying Kuramoto model and the robust almost-global stability of a parameter-varying nonautonomous system. These examples demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method and validate the theoretical results. All computational results are obtained using an open-source MATLAB implementation, as referenced in the text, thereby facilitating reproducibility of the reported examples.
tldr: This paper presents a semidefinite programming framework for constructing Lyapunov densities for nonautonomous dynamical systems on a hypertorus, with applications to synchronization and stability.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a systematic method for proving almost global stability and synchronization in time-varying nonlinear systems, which is a challenge in dynamical systems theory.
method: They use Gram matrix representations of hybrid (real-trigonometric) polynomials and introduce a block decomposition to confine density blow-up, formulating the problem as a semidefinite program.
result: The method is applied to a time-varying Kuramoto model and a parameter-varying nonautonomous system, demonstrating almost global synchronization and robust stability.
conclusion: The proposed framework is effective for constructing Lyapunov densities for nonautonomous systems on hypertori, with potential for broader applications in nonlinear control and synchronization.

title: Non-Uniform And Weighted Crossing Gates In Two-Dimensional Sandpiles
authors: Pablo Concha-Vega, Antonin Loubi\`ere, K\'evin Perrot
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining whether predicting two-dimensional sandpiles lies in [MATH] or is [MATH]-complete has been open for decades. Moore and Nilsson proved [MATH]-completeness for the three dimensional case by encoding Boolean circuits into sandpiles, but this method fails in two dimension due to the impossibility of crossing gates. In this work, we study the existence of crossing gates on non-uniform and weighted grids. We establish an equivalence between uniform weighted crossing gates and a class of simple non-uniform crossing gates, which we call primal. We also exhibit a crossing gate that inherently requires more than one crossing, rather than a single crossing as in standard constructions. Finally, we show that the equivalence between uniform weighted and primal crossings breaks down in more general settings.
tldr: This paper studies crossing gates in two-dimensional sandpile models, establishing equivalences between uniform weighted and non-uniform crossing gates.
motivation: The problem of whether predicting 2D sandpiles is in NC or P-complete has been open for decades; crossing gates are a key obstacle to encoding circuits in 2D.
method: The authors define non-uniform and weighted grids, prove an equivalence between uniform weighted crossing gates and a class of simple non-uniform crossing gates, and exhibit a crossing gate requiring multiple crossings.
result: They establish an equivalence between uniform weighted and primal non-uniform crossing gates, and show this equivalence breaks down in more general settings.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the complexity of 2D sandpiles but does not resolve the P-completeness question.

title: Mismatched Exponents For Deterministic And Randomised Noise-Guessing Decoding
authors: Henrique K. Miyamoto, Richard Combes, Sheng Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.26954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study both the deterministic and randomised variants of noise-guessing decoding in additive memoryless channels. The error and complexity exponents of such decoding schemes are analysed under mismatched decoding metrics, and then specialised to matched, [MATH]-tilted, and universal decoding metrics. The [MATH]-tilted metric is proportional to the [MATH]-th power ([MATH]) of the true noise distribution. In deterministic decoding, the tilting operation does not affect the performance: all these metrics are equivalent to the matched one ([MATH]), and are optimal for both average error and complexity. On the other hand, in randomised decoding, the matched metric is not optimal for complexity exponents; we show that the decoder needs to tune the parameter~[MATH] according to the code rate in order to simultaneously achieve both optimal exponents using a decoding metric in that family. Finally, a universal decoding metric based on the empirical entropy of the noise sequence achieves both optimal exponents, independently of the channel law and uniformly over code rates, for the deterministic and randomised variants.
tldr: This paper analyzes error and complexity exponents of noise-guessing decoding in additive memoryless channels under mismatched metrics.
motivation: To understand the performance of noise-guessing decoding when the true noise distribution is unknown or mismatched.
method: The authors study deterministic and randomized variants of noise-guessing decoding, analyzing error and complexity exponents for matched, tilted, and universal decoding metrics.
result: Deterministic decoding is optimal for all metrics; randomized decoding requires tuning the tilting parameter for optimal complexity exponents, while a universal metric achieves optimal exponents uniformly.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the trade-offs between error and complexity in mismatched decoding scenarios.
