tldr: This paper experimentally observes cluster synchronization in a biologically inspired neuronal network of chaotic electronic oscillators.
motivation: Understanding synchronization patterns in complex networks, particularly those mimicking biological neural systems, is important for neuroscience and nonlinear dynamics.
method: A network of 59 coupled chaotic electronic oscillators modeled after a dissociated rat cortical culture is used, and a spectral block method predicts cluster synchronization.
result: Cluster synchronization is observed experimentally, validating the spectral block prediction method.
conclusion: The study demonstrates the utility of spectral methods for predicting synchronization in complex networks, with potential applications to neural systems.

title: Why ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GaTe}}_{2}$ Has Higher Curie Temperature Than ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: Bomin Kim, Tumentsereg Ochirkhuyag, Dorj Odkhuu, And S. H. Rhim
abstract:
Author(s): Bomin Kim, Tumentsereg Ochirkhuyag, Dorj Odkhuu, and S. H. Rhim

Physics of [MATH] having higher Curie temperature [MATH] than [MATH] is explored theoretically in the framework of magnetic exchange interactions. [MATH] and [MATH] ar…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023333] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains why Fe3GaTe2 has a higher Curie temperature than Fe3GeTe2 using magnetic exchange interaction theory.
motivation: Understanding the origin of higher Curie temperature in Fe3GaTe2 compared to Fe3GeTe2 is important for designing two-dimensional magnetic materials.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory (DFT) are used to compute magnetic exchange parameters and Curie temperature via Monte Carlo simulations.
result: The higher Curie temperature in Fe3GaTe2 is attributed to stronger ferromagnetic exchange interactions due to the larger atomic size of Ga and its effect on the electronic structure.
conclusion: The study provides a theoretical explanation for the enhanced Curie temperature, guiding the search for high-temperature two-dimensional magnets.

authors: Michael P. Adams, Elizabeth M. Jefremovas, And Andreas Michels
abstract:

We present a symmetry-resolved classification of two-dimensional spin-flip small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) patterns arising from dilute ensembles of spherical nanoparticles hosting magnetic vortex states. Based on a linear vortex ansatz with an axially symmetric distribution of vortex axes and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023328] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper classifies spin-flip SANS patterns from magnetic vortex ensembles in spherical nanoparticles.
motivation: Understanding the angular anisotropy of magnetic vortex scattering is important for characterizing nanoscale magnetic structures.
method: The authors use a linear vortex model with axially symmetric vortex axis distribution to compute two-dimensional spin-flip SANS cross sections.
result: They provide a symmetry-resolved classification of SANS patterns based on the orientation of the applied magnetic field relative to the neutron beam.
conclusion: The classification aids in interpreting experimental SANS data from vortex-state nanoparticles.

title: Ligand-mediated Magnetic Coupling Across Metamagnetic Transitions In ${\mathrm{CrPS}}_{4}$
authors: Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli Dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, And Nicholas B. Brookes

Chromium thiophosphate ([MATH]) is a long-known material: A layered semiconducting antiferromagnet. Its recently discovered gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions, the remarkable positive and oscillating magnetoresistance as a tunnel barrier, and its Fano-resonance luminescence, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates ligand-mediated magnetic coupling across metamagnetic transitions in CrPS4, a layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor.
motivation: To understand the microscopic mechanism of metamagnetic transitions and magnetoresistance in CrPS4, which is relevant for spintronic applications.
method: Combined X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, and density functional theory calculations to probe electronic and magnetic structure.
result: Identified that ligand-mediated superexchange via sulfur atoms drives the metamagnetic transitions, with changes in Cr-S hybridization.
conclusion: The findings explain the origin of metamagnetism and provide insight into the magnetotransport properties of CrPS4.

title: Before The Cycle Is Over: Subcycle Time Refraction At Optical Frequencies
authors: Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Segal, Noa Konforty, Oded Schiller, Maxwell J. Tolchin, Tony Yasniger, Soham Saha, Ryan W. Spangler, Jon-Paul Maria, Yonatan Plotnik, and Mordechai Segev

This work demonstrates subcycle order-unity variations in the refractive index at optical frequencies and measures the time-refraction of a probe wave propagating in the modulated medium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022054] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates subcycle time refraction at optical frequencies by modulating refractive index on ultrafast timescales.
motivation: To achieve order-unity refractive index changes within an optical cycle, enabling new regimes of light-matter interaction and ultrafast control.
method: Experimental setup using a pump-probe scheme with a modulated medium to induce and measure subcycle refractive index variations.
result: Observation of subcycle time refraction with order-unity index changes at optical frequencies.
conclusion: Subcycle refractive index modulation is feasible and can be used for ultrafast optical switching and pulse shaping.

Andrew MacFarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, and Zaher Salman

We investigate the behavior of interstitial [MATH] implanted near the surface of [MATH] using [MATH]-detected nuclear magnetic resonance. We find that, unlike the muon, [MATH] does not show any signature of induced magnetism. This result is consist…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023316] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies impurity-induced magnetism and dynamics in 2H-MoTe2 using β-NMR, finding no induced magnetism for Li8 compared to muons.
motivation: To understand the behavior of interstitial impurities in transition metal dichalcogenides and their magnetic properties.
method: β-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β-NMR) is used to probe Li8 implanted near the surface of 2H-MoTe2.
result: Li8 shows no signature of induced magnetism, unlike muons, consistent with density functional theory calculations.
conclusion: The absence of magnetism for Li8 is attributed to its different electronic structure and interaction with the host.

authors: Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, And Emilia Morosan

We report the experimental discovery of bulk superconductivity in two kagome lattice compounds, [MATH] and [MATH], which were predicted through machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculati…

tldr: Machine learning and first-principles calculations predict and experimentally discover two new kagome superconductors.
motivation: To discover new kagome superconductors using machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening.
method: Machine learning models combined with first-principles calculations to screen candidate materials, followed by experimental synthesis and characterization.
result: Discovery of bulk superconductivity in YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2 with kagome lattice structure.
conclusion: The approach successfully identifies new kagome superconductors, demonstrating the power of machine learning in materials discovery.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence using the Onsager-Machlup formulation to find most probable paths and invariant sets.
motivation: Understanding turbulence transition from bistable states triggered by noise is a fundamental problem in fluid dynamics.
method: The authors apply the Onsager-Machlup functional to a stochastic dynamical system to compute most probable transition paths and identify invariant sets.
result: They characterize the most probable paths and invariant sets governing the noise-induced transition to turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the role of noise in triggering turbulence transitions, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Current-induced Successive Structural Phase Transitions Beyond Thermal Equilibrium In Single-crystal ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$
authors: Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Ichiro Terasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-hisa Arima, and Ichiro Terasaki

Using synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy, current-induced structural phase transitions in single-crystal vanadium dioxide are investigated. Successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases are observed, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion inaccessible under thermal equilibrium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022050] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports current-induced structural phase transitions in VO2 single crystals, revealing nonequilibrium metallic phases not accessible under thermal equilibrium.
motivation: To understand how electric currents can drive structural phase transitions beyond thermal equilibrium, potentially enabling new pathways to control material properties.
method: Synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy were used to characterize structural changes in single-crystal VO2 under applied currents.
result: Successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases were observed, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion.
conclusion: Current-induced effects can produce structural phases that are inaccessible via thermal equilibrium, highlighting the role of non-thermal pathways in phase transitions.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, identifying transient dynamical bottlenecks that cause training instabilities.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in neural networks can improve training stability and efficiency.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of recurrent networks, identifying ghost points as transient bottlenecks and analyzing their dynamics.
result: The ghost mechanism provides a theoretical explanation for abrupt learning and suggests ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism is a key underlying process for abrupt learning in recurrent networks, with implications for improving training.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, particularly regarding time-reversal symmetry breaking.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe the magnetic properties and critical behavior.
result: Observation of a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and evidence for hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The kagome ice compound HoAgGe exhibits a complex magnetic ground state with hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking, characterized by a 3D XY universality class transition.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To find and characterize materials with intrinsic flat bands that can host strongly correlated electron states without the need for moiré engineering.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on layered transition-metal oxyhalides, combined with theoretical calculations.
result: Observation of flat bands that are stable at room temperature and tunable via material composition.
conclusion: These materials provide a promising platform for studying strongly correlated physics in a naturally occurring, room-temperature stable system.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between multiple ferroic orders and the formation of complex domain walls in a material with a uniform ferro-rotational state.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to study the material Ni2Mo3O8.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational degrees of freedom.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the dipolar nematic state may explain their unique properties.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling or experimental characterization to identify and describe the nematic ordering.
result: They report the existence of a dipolar nematic phase in relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: This nematic ordering is key to understanding relaxor behavior, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics.

abstract:

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: To understand the nature of long-lived hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems and their unique excitations.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation combined with resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe polaronic and phononic excitations in Pr0.67Ca0.33MnO3.
result: A long-lived hidden phase with distinct polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium is observed.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can induce metastable hidden phases with novel properties in manganites, relevant for non-equilibrium control of correlated materials.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The review surveys various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The paper summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open questions in the field.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods for internal conversion are needed to advance applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the Standard Model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them, such as precision measurements and symmetry tests.
result: The review summarizes the current status of experimental constraints on various spin-dependent exotic interactions and outlines future directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
