conclusion: The work provides insights into the design principles of multistable gene circuits.

title: Influence Of Visual Field Offset On Collective Behavior: An Exploration Using The Two-dimensional Vicsek Model
authors: Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, And Subhradeep Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Poorendra Ramlall, Sachit Butail, and Subhradeep Roy

This study investigates the influence of visual field offset—a restricted field of vision positioned at a fixed angle from an agent's heading direction—on collective behavior using the Vicsek model. This offset shapes an agent's ability to perceive and respond to neighbors, thereby impacting overall…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064409] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how a fixed visual field offset affects collective motion in the Vicsek model, a classical model of self-propelled particles.
motivation: Understanding how sensory limitations, such as a restricted field of view, influence emergent collective behavior in animal groups or robotic swarms.
method: Numerical simulations of the two-dimensional Vicsek model with agents having a visual field offset—a fixed angular shift between heading and visual direction.
result: The visual field offset alters the onset and nature of collective motion, affecting order parameters and clustering dynamics.
conclusion: Visual field offset is a significant parameter in collective behavior, with implications for biological and robotic systems.

title: Enhanced Plasma Production By Ambipolar Electric Fields In Convergent Magnetic Fields
authors: Kazunori Takahashi, Christine Charles, Rod W. Boswell, And Antonella Caldarelli
abstract:
Author(s): Kazunori Takahashi, Christine Charles, Rod W. Boswell, and Antonella Caldarelli

Controlled unidirectional remote plasma production in a radio-frequency (rf) plasma source is demonstrated by placing magnetic nozzle throat several tens of centimeters away from the rf antenna, where a local density peak forms near the throat. The experiment indicates that the dominant electron ene…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies plasma production in a convergent magnetic field using ambipolar electric fields, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand and control remote plasma production for applications like electric propulsion.
method: Experimental measurements of plasma density and electron energy in a radio-frequency plasma source with a magnetic nozzle.
result: A local density peak forms near the magnetic nozzle throat, indicating enhanced plasma production via ambipolar electric fields.
conclusion: Ambipolar electric fields in convergent magnetic fields can efficiently produce remote plasmas, relevant for thruster design.

title: Proof-of-principle Experiment Of A Beam Extraction Over Millions Of Turns Using Stable Resonance Islands And Bent Crystal
authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti
abstract:
Author(s): D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. Van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, and G. Franchetti

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. This work reports on the successful proof-of-principle experiment conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, in which stable islands and a bent crystal were employed to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, thereby emulating slow extraction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022055] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a proof-of-principle experiment for beam extraction using resonance islands and a bent crystal at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron.
motivation: To develop a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators, which could improve efficiency and reduce activation of components.
method: The experiment combines particle trapping in stable resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal to split and channel a circulating proton beam onto an absorber.
result: Successful proof-of-principle demonstration of beam extraction over millions of turns using the combined technique.
conclusion: The method shows promise for low-loss slow extraction in high-intensity accelerators, but further development is needed for practical application.

title: Plasma Flow Generation And Particle Acceleration From Expanding Magnetic Bubbles
authors: Yang Zhang, Brandon K. Russell, Geoffrey Pomraning, Lan Gao, Xiaocan Li, Adam Stanier, William Daughton, Chuanfei Dong, Liang Wang, Peiyun Shi, Kian Orr, And Hantao Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Zhang, Brandon K. Russell, Geoffrey Pomraning, Lan Gao, Xiaocan Li, Adam Stanier, William Daughton, Chuanfei Dong, Liang Wang, Peiyun Shi, Kian Orr, and Hantao Ji

Impulsive plasma dynamics in the laboratory are often driven by rising electric currents, yet their quantitative plasma response has not been well established. By means of fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations and laser-driven capacitor-coil experiments, we show that a rising current expels pla…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies plasma flow generation and particle acceleration from expanding magnetic bubbles using simulations and experiments.
motivation: To understand impulsive plasma dynamics driven by rising electric currents, which are important for astrophysical and laboratory plasmas.
method: Fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations and laser-driven capacitor-coil experiments.
result: A rising current expels plasma and generates fast flows and energetic particles.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into plasma dynamics in astrophysical contexts and laboratory setups.

title: Leidenfrost Hydrogels: Elastic Surface-wave Instability And Sustained Bouncing
authors: Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, And James E. Sprittles
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, and James E. Sprittles

This work investigates the oscillatory dynamics and subsequent sustained bouncing behavior of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a phenomenon that has received little theoretical attention to date. Building on previous approaches toward drop impacts and Leidenfrost drops, a computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022052] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the oscillatory dynamics and sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a soft matter physics phenomenon.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, which has received little theoretical attention.
method: A computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the energy injection mechanism.
result: The model reveals an elastic surface-wave instability that sustains bouncing.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into the sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels.

title: Tracking Phase Synchronization Between Flagella In The Time-frequency Domain Resolves Photophobic Response
authors: Lucas Federspiel, Jorge Arrieta, Marco Polin, Françoise Argoul, And Antoine Allard
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Federspiel, Jorge Arrieta, Marco Polin, Françoise Argoul, and Antoine Allard

The unicellular microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (CR) is well known for its biflagellated swimming in response to light stimuli. This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023294] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flagellar synchronization in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii using time-frequency analysis to characterize photophobic response.
motivation: Understanding how microalgae coordinate flagella after light stimuli is important for biophysics and cellular behavior.
method: The authors use time-frequency domain analysis to track phase synchronization between two flagella from high-speed video recordings.
result: They quantify resynchronization dynamics after a photoshock and identify characteristic timescales.
conclusion: The method provides a robust way to study flagellar coordination and its response to environmental cues.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts its application in areas like flow control. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate super-resonance, achieving a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance.
result: Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new paradigm for resonant systems, with potential applications in flow control and beyond.

title: Erratum: Opposite Effects Of The Rotational And Translational Energy On The Rates Of Ion-Molecule Reactions Near 0 K: The ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{NH}}_{3}$ And ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}^{+}+{\mathrm{ND}}_{3}$ Reactions [Phys. Rev. X 14, 011034 (2024)]
authors: Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, And Frédéric Merkt
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Hahn, David Schlander, Valentina Zhelyazkova, and Frédéric Merkt
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 029901] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on low-temperature ion-molecule reaction rates, with no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The original paper studied rotational and translational energy effects on ion-molecule reactions near 0 K; the erratum corrects errors in that work.
method: The erratum likely corrects experimental or theoretical details from the original study.
result: The erratum provides corrected results for the D2+ + NH3 and D2+ + ND3 reactions.
conclusion: The corrected findings refine the understanding of low-temperature ion-molecule reaction dynamics.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Giomi

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: A continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces is formulated analogously to the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new mathematical description of metashell mechanics, enabling design principles for metamaterials.
conclusion: The work offers a different path for materials design by linking mechanics to quantum-like equations.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and connect to bulk hydrogel behavior via a force-response model.
result: They identify how protein unfolding and refolding cycles contribute to fatigue fracture and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a molecular-level understanding of fatigue in hydrogels and offers a design principle for tougher soft materials.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, and Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films induced by mesopore change, focusing on wood-derived films and vapor training.
motivation: To improve the plasticity and shaping of wood-derived films for practical applications.
method: A vapor training process is used to induce mesopore changes in nanocrystal films.
result: The process leads to improved plasticity and better shaping of the films.
conclusion: The vapor training method effectively enhances the mechanical properties of wood-derived nanocrystal films.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, and Ulrich S. Schwarz

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding how mechanical forces at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets lead to cell extrusion is important for tissue biology and disease.
method: The authors develop a 3D bubbly vertex model to simulate curved epithelial sheets and analyze cell shape changes and extrusion events.
result: They find that cells at topological defects experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion, and the model captures key features of cell dynamics.
conclusion: The bubbly vertex model provides insights into the role of geometry and mechanics in epithelial cell extrusion.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, Van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, and Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: To understand the hydrodynamics of microbial motility, which has biological implications for nutrient uptake and predator-prey interactions.
method: Experimental three-dimensional flow measurements using particle tracking velocimetry around a free-swimming alga.
result: The flow field exhibits complex three-dimensional structures not captured by previous 2D models.
conclusion: Microscopic organisms generate richer flow patterns than previously thought, impacting our understanding of microhydrodynamics and microbial ecology.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key mechanisms and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A review of hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and QCD.
motivation: To understand strong interaction mechanisms such as quark confinement and gluon binding through charmonium decays and searches for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BaBar, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights recent advances from BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: Hadron spectroscopy in open-charm channels provides crucial tests of QCD and continues to yield new insights.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its contributions to various scientific fields.
method: The editorial compiles three colloquia that review the observatory's achievements.
result: The paper highlights Arecibo's revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has left a lasting legacy in multiple areas of science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To document the contributions of the Arecibo planetary radar system to planetary science and its role in supporting space exploration.
method: The paper presents a historical overview of radar techniques and summarizes key observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo radar provided unique subsurface and surface data that complemented other observations and guided in situ missions.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary radar, and its loss leaves a gap in capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the scientific legacy of the Arecibo Observatory following its collapse.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Highlights Arecibo's major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's unique capabilities and upgrades enabled groundbreaking discoveries across multiple fields.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize the scientific contributions of the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research over its 50-year operation.
method: Review of incoherent scatter radar technique and results from Arecibo's radar, lidar, optical, and satellite instruments.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal atom layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are highlighted.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory enabled unique studies of geospace, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud microphysics.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate controlled turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising platform to address the precipitation bottleneck, but further work is needed to fully connect lab results to atmospheric clouds.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare, multimessenger events that can reveal physics of the supernova engine and neutron star formation.
method: The paper summarizes recent supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, along with detection and parameter estimation methods for ground-based interferometers.
result: It presents the latest progress in modeling and detection strategies for gravitational waves from core collapse supernovae.
conclusion: Gravitational wave observations from a Galactic supernova would provide unique insights into the central engine and neutron star physics.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a cosmological observation that challenges the standard ΛCDM model, and has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the cosmic microwave background dipole.
method: Analysis of radio galaxy and quasar catalogs to measure the dipole anisotropy and compare it with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, challenging the standard ΛCDM model.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require new physics beyond ΛCDM.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their effects on galaxy and large-scale structure formation.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter by testing self-interacting dark matter scenarios against astrophysical observations.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes results from simulations and observations of dark matter halos, galaxies, and large-scale structures.
result: It summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections from various astrophysical probes.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable model, but further observational and theoretical work is needed to distinguish it from collisionless dark matter.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a review of viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery sensitivities for multiple search channels at the HL-LHC.
result: The paper provides an overview of the remaining viable supersymmetric scenarios and their expected signatures at the HL-LHC.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains a compelling framework, but its discovery at the HL-LHC depends on the specific model and requires dedicated searches across diverse channels.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma effects, and diagnostics like neutrinos and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar properties and testing solar models.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and atomic effects in the solar interior.
result: It summarizes advances in nuclear reaction cross sections, plasma screening, and the impact on solar neutrino fluxes and helioseismic predictions.
conclusion: The updated nuclear physics inputs improve the agreement between solar models and observations, but some discrepancies remain.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.

tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and self-consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating all data up to the end of 2022.
result: A new set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, along with their uncertainties.
conclusion: The 2022 CODATA values supersede previous sets and serve as the internationally accepted reference for fundamental constants.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: A review of gas bubble dynamics in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and surfactants.
motivation: Gas bubbles are important in many natural and industrial processes, but their dynamics are complex due to deformability and interactions.
method: The paper reviews recent advances in experimental and theoretical studies of bubble motion, including effects of turbulence, rheology, and surfactants.
result: Key advances over the past 20 years are summarized, highlighting the influence of liquid properties and flow conditions on bubble behavior.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can reveal conditions in the first second after the Big Bang, which are opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models for gravitational wave sources (phase transitions, topological defects) and detection strategies.
result: Summarizes potential signals and detection methods for stochastic gravitational waves from early universe events.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique probe of the early universe, but detection requires future experiments.

title: Nucleation Of Adamantane Clusters In Weakly Ionised Plasmas: Dispersion Cohesion, Surface Energy, And Charging
authors: Johannes Fiedler And Justas Zalieckas
abstract: The formation of molecular clusters in low-temperature plasmas is governed by an intricate interplay of dispersion interactions, electrostatic charging, and surface energetics. While chemical growth pathways have been extensively studied, the role of non-chemical interactions in determining characteristic cluster sizes remains poorly understood. In this work, we develop a unified free-energy framework for molecular clusters embedded in weakly ionised Ar/H plasmas. The approach combines first-principles calculations of the molecular polarisability of adamantane with a dielectric description of the plasma response, including collisional damping and plasma screening. Dispersion interactions are treated as a bulk-like cohesive contribution with a physically motivated microscopic cutoff, while electrostatic charging is described within floating-potential theory. We show that, for realistic discharge parameters, the total free energy does not generally exhibit an effective equilibrium radius. Instead, the free-energy landscape is characterised by a nucleation barrier with an effective critical radius separating subcritical clusters from downhill growth. By mapping this nucleation threshold scale as a function of pressure, electron temperature, and gas composition, we demonstrate that plasma conditions provide a systematic control over the nucleation scale. Our results suggest that experimentally observed steady cluster sizes in weakly ionised plasmas are governed by kinetic balance rather than free-energy minimisation, and that gas composition and plasma parameters can be used as effective control knobs for early-stage cluster formation.
tldr: This paper studies the nucleation of adamantane clusters in weakly ionized plasmas using a free-energy framework, focusing on dispersion interactions and charging effects.
motivation: To understand the role of non-chemical interactions in determining cluster sizes in low-temperature plasmas, which is poorly understood.
method: Develops a unified free-energy model combining first-principles polarisability calculations with a dielectric plasma description, including collisional damping and screening.
result: The free-energy landscape shows a nucleation barrier with a critical radius; no equilibrium radius exists; cluster sizes are governed by kinetic balance.
conclusion: Plasma conditions (pressure, electron temperature, gas composition) can control nucleation scale, but steady cluster sizes arise from kinetics, not free-energy minimization.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for analyzing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills theory.
motivation: To understand nontrivial physics beyond planarity in gauge/gravity duality by studying correlators involving giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: Identifies a hidden defect extension of 10d conformal symmetry and extracts the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel double-particle operators.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. Allan deviation analysis indicated that the minimum detection limits (MDLs) for CH4 and C2H2 reached 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, with normalized noise-equivalent absorption coefficients of 5.09 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2 and 6.18 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a novel optical detection method using orthogonal phase modulation and Lissajous mode decoupling in light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy for real-time multi-component gas sensing.
motivation: Real-time multi-component gas sensing is important for environmental monitoring and industrial safety, but existing methods suffer from channel crosstalk and complexity.
method: Two lasers are modulated with same frequency but 45° phase difference, co-excite a quartz tuning fork, and the piezoelectric signal is orthogonally demodulated via lock-in amplifier to decouple gas concentration information.
result: The sensor achieves linear responses for CH4 and C2H2 with low systematic errors (0.54% and 0.79%) and detection limits of 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm respectively.
conclusion: The proposed OPM-LITES sensor provides a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection with a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling.
